senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to be cut off, separated, v. Ges. Hebr. Dict.12 s. v.; cmp. פָּרַשׁ,] to be, become pure, sacred, holy.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:1:13">Y. Sabb. III, 5ᵈ</cite> bot.; ib. IV, end, 7ᵃ <he>ק׳ עליו היום</he> the day became holy upon him, i.e. the Sabbath commenced while he was engaged in doing something.

<cite ref="Mishnah Meilah 2:8">Meïl. II, 8</cite> (<cite ref="Meilah 10a:5">10ᵃ</cite>) <he>קָדְשׁוּ בכלים</he> (Talm. ed. <he>קדשן</he>) after they have become sacred by being put in a sacred vessel (v. infra); <cite ref="Shevuot 11a:3">Shebu. 11ᵃ</cite> (Ms. F. <he>קידשן</he>).
<cite ref="Bekhorot 4b:22">Bekh. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>קדשו בכורות וכ׳</he> the firstborn in the desert were consecrated; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to sanctify, esp. ק׳ שם שמים, or ק׳ את השם to sanctify the name of the Lord, to manifest fidelity to religion by noble deeds, by martyrdom &c.
units: <cite ref="Sotah 10b">Sot. 10ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sotah 36b:10">36ᵇ</cite> <he>יוסף שק׳ שם וכ׳</he> Joseph who sanctified the name … in secret (when he resisted temptation); <he>יהודה שק׳ וכ׳</he> Judah who sanctified … in public (when he admitted his guilt, <cite ref="Genesis 38:26">Gen. XXXVIII, 26</cite>); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to sanctify, consecrate; to purify, keep pure.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 17a:7">Ber. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>טהר וקַדֵּשׁ עצמך מכל וכ׳</he> keep thyself clean and pure (aloof) from every guilt &c.

<cite ref="Yoma 39a">Yoma 39ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 11:44">Lev. XI, 44</cite>) … <he>אדם מְקַדֵּשׁ מְקַדְּשִׁין אותו הרבה</he> if a man sanctifies himself a little (trains himself to self-restraint), they (the divine agencies) will help him much to sanctify him; <he>מלמטה מקדשין אותו מלמעלה</he> if he (sanctifies himself) below, they will sanctify him from above; <he>בעולם הזה מקדשין וכ׳</he> he in this world, they will declare him holy in the hereafter.
<cite ref="Yevamot 20a:15">Yeb. 20ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>קדש עצמך במותר לך</he> sanctify thyself by self-restraint from what is permitted to thee.

<cite ref="Chagigah 3b:10">Ḥag. 3ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>קִדְּשָׁהּ לשעתה</he>, v. <cite ref="S00123"><he>קְדוּשָּׁה</he></cite>. Sebu. 15ᵃ … <he>כל הכלים מְקַדַּשְׁתָּן</he> as regards all vessels that Moses made, the ointing of them gave them their sacred character; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 16b:5">Snh. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>מקדשן</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Menachot 95b:13">Men. 95ᵇ</cite> <he>תנור מְקַדֵּשׁ</he> the oven (the baking of the showbread) gives it its sacred character.

<cite ref="Menachot 100a:17">Ib. 100ᵃ</cite> <he>כלי שרת מְקַדְּשִׁין</he> the vessels of the service consecrate (the things put into them); a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְקוּדָּשׁ</he>; f. <he>מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת</he>; pl. <he>מְקוּדָּשִׁים</he> &c.
Sabb. 55ᵃ (ref. to Ez. IX, 6) א״ת מקדשי אלא מְקוּדָּשַׁי וכ׳ read not miḳdashi (my sanctuary) but m’ḳuddashai (my sanctified ones), that means those who fulfilled the whole Law &c.; Ab. Zar. 4ᵃ.

<cite ref="Zevachim 115b:2">Zeb. 115ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 68:36">Ps. LXVIII, 36</cite> <he>מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ</he>) read <he>מִמְּקוּדָּשֶׁיךָ וכ׳</he> ‘from thy sanctified ones’, when the Lord passes judgment on his holy servants &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (with, or sub., ידיו ורגליו) to wash hands and feet prior to a sacred act.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:6">Yoma III, 6</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 4:5">Ib. IV, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Yoma 22a:6">Ib. 22ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to prepare the water of lustration (Num. XIX).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Parah 6:1">Par. VI, 1</cite> <he>המקדש ונפל הקִדּוּשׁ על ידו</he> if he prepares the lustration, and some of the consecrated water falls upon his hand.
<cite ref="Mishnah Parah 6:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>נוטל ומקדש</he> he may take (of the ashes) and prepare the water with them.
<cite ref="Mishnah Parah 6:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>המקדש בשוקת וכ׳</he> he who puts ashes into a large vessel of water; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (of seasons) to proclaim the sanctity of esp.,
(ק׳ החדש) to proclaim in court that the new month had begun (v. infra).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:7">R. Hash. II, 7</cite> <he>אם לא … אין מקדשין אותו שכבד קִדְּשׁוּהוּ שמים</he> unless the new moon is seen in its due time (on the evening of the twenty-ninth day), no announcement is made, for the heavens have already proclaimed it (and the new month begins with the thirty-first day).

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 24a:9-11">Ib. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>בין כך שנים אתה מקדש וכ׳ …</he> in neither case is the ceremony of announcement required, for we read (<cite ref="Leviticus 25:10">Lev. XXV, 10</cite>), ‘ye shall sanctify the fiftieth year’, years thou must sanctify &c.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:28">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> <he>אני ואתם נְקַדֵּשׁ את החדש</he> I and you, let us (as a court) proclaim the month (of Nisan); a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab.

R. Hash. II, 7 ראש ב״ד אומר מק׳ וכ׳ the president of the court says, ‘(the new month is) proclaimed’, and all the people say after him, ‘proclaimed, proclaimed.’ Ib. III, 1 נחקרו … ולא הספיקו לומר מק׳ וכ׳ when the witnesses were examined, and the court had no time to say m’ḳuddash before night set in; a. e.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: ק׳ השבת, היום to pronounce the sanctity of the Sabbath, the Holy Day &c., to recite the Sabbath or the festive benediction (over wine), to say Ḳiddush.
units: Pes. 105ᵃ מי שלא ק׳ בע״ש מקדש וכ׳ he who fails to bless the Sabbath on the Sabbath eve, may do so during the entire day. Ib. 106ᵇ טעם אינו מקדש if a man tasted something without Ḳiddush, he must not bless the Sabbath; Ib. 107ᵃ טעם מקדש even if he has tasted something, he must bless the Sabbath. Ib. כגון זה ראוי לקַדֵּשׁ עליו a beverage like this is fit for Ḳiddush; a. fr.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: ק׳ אשה [to consecrate a woman,]
to betroth (expl.
units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 2b:2">Kidd. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>לישנא דרבנן דאסר לה … כהקדש</he> the rabbinical term, in place of the Biblical <he>קנה</he>,—because he makes her forbidden to others like a consecrated object, v. <cite ref="E00789"><he>הֶקְדֵּשׁ</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 2:1">Kidd. II, 1</cite> <he>האיש מקדש בו וכ׳</he> a man may betroth a woman either in person or through a deputy.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 41a:5">Ib. 41ᵃ</cite> <he>אסור לאדם שיְקַדֵּשׁ … עד וכ׳</he> a man is forbidden to betroth a woman to himself, before he has seen her.

<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 2:4">Ib. II, 4</cite> <he>האומר … צא וקַדֵּשׁ … והלך וקִדְּשָׁהּ וכ׳</he> if a man said to his deputy, go and betroth to me that certain woman in that certain place, and he went and betrothed her in a different place, she is not betrothed (the betrothal is invalid); a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת</he>; pl. <he>מְקוּדָּשׁוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 2:4">Ib.</cite> <he>הרי זו מק׳</he> in such a case the betrothal is binding. Ib. 7; a. fr.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: (of the father of a minor נַעֲרָה) to accept a betrothal in behalf of one’s daughter. Ib. 1 האיש מקדש את בתו וכ׳ a man may accept his daughter’s betrothal, if she is a naʿărah, either in person or through a deputy. Ib. 41ᵃ אסור לאדם שיקדש את בתו וכ׳ a man is forbidden to betroth his daughter as a child, (but must wait,) until she is grown up and says, I like this man; a. fr.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: to cause a thing to be prohibited, esp. (by ref. to Deut. XXII, 9) by planting seeds in a vineyard, or vines among seeds; to cause condemnation.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 4:5">Kil. IV, 5</cite> <he>הזורע … ק׳ שורה אחת</he> if a person sows within four cubits of a vineyard, he has caused the condemnation of one row of vines.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 5:5">Ib. V, 5</cite> <he>הרי זה מקדש ארבעים וכ׳</he> he has made forty-five vines forbidden.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 7:2">Ib. VII, 2</cite> <he>גפן … ואינה מְקַדֶּשֶׁת</he> to plant seeds near a dried-up vine is forbidden, but it (the vine) does not cause the condemnation of the seeds.

<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 7:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>אלו אוסרין ולא מְקַדְּשִׁין</he> the following plants make the planting of seeds in their neighborhood forbidden, but do not cause condemnation of the seeds, if planted, or their own condemnation.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 7:5">Ib. 5</cite> <he>אין אדם מקדש דבר וכ׳</he> no man can cause condemnation of a thing not his own.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 7:5">Ib.</cite> <he>הרי זה ק׳ וכ׳</he> he has caused the condemnation of his neighbor’s seeds and must pay damages; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be sanctified, glorified as holy.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 79a:7-9">Yeb. 79ᵃ</cite> <he>מוטב … ויִתְקַדֵּשׁ שם וכ׳</he> let a letter of the Law be uprooted (disregarded), but let the name of God be sanctified in public. Tanḥ. Sh’mini 1 <he>מִתְקַדֵּשׁ אני שם במכבדי</he> there (at the dedication of the Tabernacle) I shall be sanctified by (the death of) those that honor me.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 12">Lev. R. s. 12</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be consecrated, dedicated; (of the New Moon) to be proclaimed.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 21b:6">R. Hash. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>יכול … עד שיִתְקַדְּשׁוּ וכ׳</he> you may have thought, as well as the Sabbath is to be disregarded (by the witnesses travelling to the seat of the court), until they (the months) are proclaimed, it may also be disregarded (by the messengers carrying the announcement), until they are established.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:28">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> <he>היה הכהן … והכלי מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת</he> the priest received in it some sacred object, by which the vessel was consecrated; <he>וכלי חול מִתְקַדֵּשׁ</he> and a profane vessel became sacred.
<cite ref="Shevuot 15a:10">Shebu. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>אין העזרה מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת וכ׳</he> the Temple hall was not consecrated, until the priests ate therein the remnants of the meal-offering.
<cite ref="Shevuot 16a:6">Ib. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>תחתונה נִתְקַדְּשָׁה בכל אלו</he> the lower reservoir became consecrated through all these (ceremonies mentioned); a. fr.

senses.gloss: (of mixed seeds) to be condemnable, condemned.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 7:7">Kil. VII, 7</cite> <he>מאימתי … מתקדשת</he> from what time are seeds of grain (planted among vines) to be condemned? <cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 7:7">Ib.</cite> <he>אין מִתְקַדְּשׁוֹת</he> are not to be condemned; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be betrothed.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 2:1">Kidd. II, 1</cite> <he>האשה מתקדשת בה וכ׳</he> a woman may be betrothed in person or through her deputy.

<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 2:1">Ib.</cite> <he>האומר … הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לי וכ׳</he> if a man says to a woman, be betrothed to me with this fig. Ib. 45ᵇ <he>נִתְקַדְּשָׁה לדעת אביה וניסת וכ׳</he> if she (the minor) was betrothed with her father’s consent, but was married without it; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to sanctify one’s self. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. II, Par. 2 מי שהוא עתיד להִתְקַדֵּשׁ he that is ready to sanctify himself (by vowing a sacrifice).
to be sanctified; to become consecrated.
units: <cite ref="Temurah 14a:57">Tem. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>כאן לִיקָּדֵשׁ כאן ליקרב</he> in the one case it refers to being consecrated (by being put in a sacred vessel), in the other to being offered.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 4b:23">Bekh. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>הוֹזהרו … ליקדש</he> they were admonished concerning the firstborn, that they be consecrated; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be betrothed.
units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 48a:5">Kidd. 48ᵃ</cite> if she says, <he>עשה לי … ואֶקָּדֵשׁ וכ׳</he> make for me chains &c., and I shall be betrothed unto thee.

senses.gloss: to cause sanctification.
units: <cite ref="Zevachim 115b:13">Zeb. 115ᵇ</cite> <he>לא מתו … להַקְדִּישׁ שמו וכ׳</he> thy (Aaron’s) sons died only in order to give thee an opportunity to sanctify the name of the Lord.

senses.gloss: to sanctify, dedicate an object as Temple property (Lev. XXVII, 14-24).
units: Arakh. VI, 2 המַקְדִּישׁ נכסיו וכ׳ if a person dedicates his property to the Temple, but owes his (divorced) wife her k’thubah (כְּתוּבָּה) &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 7:1">Ib. VII, 1</cite> <he>אין מַקְדִּישִׁין לפני היובל וכ׳</he> you cannot dedicate landed property within less than two or three years before the jubilee.
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 7:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>הִקְדִּישָׁהּ וגאלה</he> if he dedicated and then redeemed it.
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 7:5">Ib. 5</cite> <he>אין אדם מַקְדִּישׁ דבר וכ׳</he> nobody can dedicate a thing not belonging to him.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 7:2">B. Kam. VII, 2</cite>; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to be dedicated, consecrated.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Meilah 2:8">Meïl. II, 8</cite> <he>המנחות … משהוּקְדָּשׁוּ</he> the law concerning misappropriation of sacred things applies to meal-offerings as soon as they have been dedicated.

<cite ref="Mishnah Meilah 2:1">Ib. 1</cite> <he>משהוּקְדָּשָׁה</he> as soon as it has been designated for a sin-offering; a. fr.—Part. <cite ref="M00587"><he>מוּקְדָּשׁ</he></cite>; f. <he>מוּקְדֶּשֶׁת</he>; pl. <he>מוּקְדָּשִׁים</he> &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 5:6">Ned. V, 6</cite> (<cite ref="Nedarim 48a:7">48ᵃ</cite>) <he>אם … הרי הם מוק׳ לשמים</he> if they are mine, be they dedicated to the Lord.

<cite ref="Nedarim 48a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>כל מתנה … מקודשת אינה מתנה</he> (read: <he>מוקדשׁת</he>) a gift which is not made so that if the recipient dedicates it to sacred use, it is dedicated, is no gift.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 5:1">Bekh. V, 1</cite> <he>כל פסולי המוק׳</he> all dedicated sacrifices which became unfit for the altar; a. fr.
